written.myAnswer: Archaea lack peptidoglycan in their cell walls, have distinctive membrane lipids, and their rRNA is more similar to that of eukaryotes than to bacteria. Some live in extreme environments. Bacteria have peptidoglycan cell walls, occur in many environments, and include both beneficial and disease-causing species.

Both Archaea and Bacteria are prokaryotic. Archaea lack peptidoglycan in their cell walls, have distinctive membrane lipids, and have rRNA more similar to eukaryotes; some live in extreme environments. Bacteria have peptidoglycan cell walls, are widespread, and include beneficial as well as disease-causing forms.
